title: ANIME WORKOUTS - Can you train like a Baki character? A Grappler Baki Training Glossary
summary: NH looks at the training scenes in Grappler Baki for real lessons: recovery (Baki versus Jack's overtraining and steroids), choosing a routine you enjoy, long sessions with daily consistency, training to failure (a minor character's brutal excavation feat), and progressive overload, symbolised by Baki beating soldiers from weakest to strongest. He says copying anime training literally won't get you jacked, but the drive it inspires helps.
claims: Shonen training arcs got him into exercise and are still his favourite part of manga
Copying anime characters' training will not make you jacked because the regimens are deliberately exaggerated
Jack trained masochistically without rest and could only gain with steroids; Baki respected recovery and got results
Bodybuilding needs willpower plus the curiosity to try new methods and analyse the results
The best routine is the one you enjoy and stick to, not the most optimal on paper; don't be afraid to go your own way
One summer he trained 5-6 hours every day with a feverish drive to progress
Don't artificially cap workout length; long sessions are fine as long as you recover and keep progressing
Someone who trains 4 hours twice a week will be outdone by someone who trains 2 hours six times a week
Consistency needs a regimented schedule for eating, resting and training
Long hours without intensity lead to stagnation; go to failure with weights that challenge you without biting off more than you can chew
Volume, frequency and intensity are wasted unless they are scheduled to produce progressive overload
Ease into a new workload instead of going in guns blazing, which risks injury or burnout
The order of exercises in a session matters as much as which patterns you choose
